newsitem.title: USA: U.S. State Dept. condemns Peruvian rebels.
newsitem.headline: U.S. State Dept. condemns Peruvian rebels.

text.p: The U.S. State Department Wednesday condemned Peruvian rebels who laid siege to the Japanese ambassador's home in Lima and threatened to kill at least 200 hostages.
"We condemn this and all terrorist acts," said State Department spokesman John Dinger.
"We hope the incident can quickly be brought to a conclusion, that all hostages will be released safely, and that the perpetrators will be brought to justice."
Dinger said the department was in "close contact" with Peru's government through the country's embassy here in Washington and through the U.S. ambassador to Peru.
Dinger declined to say whether any Americans were among those being held hostage, explaining that it is U.S. government policy not to confirm the presence of U.S. citizens in hostage situations.
He did note that the host government -- in this case Peru -- alway's has primary responsibility for dealing with terrorist incidents.
